notes.title: Visual enhancements and added voiceover
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Detectives![/h1]

After almost exactly one month, we're back with another update. This time we're bringing [b]two major improvements[/b] to Timeshift Detective which we're happy to announce.

First, we [b]freshened up the visual style[/b] a bit, overhauling how we utilize lighting and colors to create a more [b]atmospheric[/b] and [b]moody environment[/b].
You can see some before and after examples of the visual update below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44742517/7c088a6c5ac39be976fbb7bb9227876e619878e2.gif[/img]

Second, we added a full [b]voiceover[/b] to each and every dialogue or monologue in the game. This lends some [b]more personality[/b] to our characters and reduces the amount of mandatory reading for those of you less inclined to do so. Unfortunately, we can't show you that in a gif. But hopefully you won't have to wait too long before we can present you some video content including audio bits!

[h2]But wait, there is more:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Made Bernstein's apartment more chaotic
[*] Added the Mysteries UI, making it easier to remember unsolved mysteries
[*] Added the option to skip cutscenes and previously heard dialogues
[*] Added a contextual marker to questions in the notebook which indicates an unresolved confrontation
[*] A location's name is now shown after entering it
[*] The pause menu now uses regular gameplay as its background
[*] Tweaked the texts of some dialogues
[*] Various bugfixes
[/list]

notes.title: Timeshift Detective says "Hello!"
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Timeshift Detective community,[/h1]

[b]thank you[/b] for the early interest in our game! We hope you'll like what you see and we eagerly await your feedback and toughts on the game so far.

We want to use these Steam events to keep you updated on the progress of the game's development and other exciting news surrounding it. As this is our first announcement on Steam, we want to give you a quick rundown of the current state of the game (as of version 0.2.3):

[list]
[*] One fully playable murder mystery case.
[*] 2 locations containing many objects that can be examined in different ways.
[*] 6 persons that can be questioned, resulting in over 60 dialogues.
[*] A notebook which automatically tracks relevant clues and unlocked questions.
[*] Mysteries, which need to be solved by collecting and then combining the correct clues.
[*] Confrontations, interactive dialogues where the player needs to pick the right clues in order to progress the conversation.
[*] LightOS, a virtual operating system containing files, web pages and messenger chats, that can be hacked into to continue the investigation digitally.
[/list]

If you've read this far, we assume you are probably interested in playing our game. We're always interested in player feedback, so if you're eager to step into the yellow trenchcoat of Harrison Steel and can't wait to start investigating, feel free to contact us via the Neox Games Discord server, where we will periodically hand out keys to our closed beta!
